rounds.proof_sketch: Launch parameters: dim3 block(BLOCK_SIZE) where BLOCK_SIZE=512 for dim_size=16384. This means blockDim.x=512, blockDim.y=1, blockDim.z=1. Original loop: stride=blockDim.x=512 (each thread handles 32 elements). Mutated loop: stride=blockDim.y=1 (thread 0 iterates 16384 times, thread 1 iterates 16383 times, etc.). However, for any element i, ALL threads that write to batch_output[i] compute the identical value: val=batch_input[i], result=val-log_sum_exp. Since log_sum_exp is computed from shared memory (identical for all threads) and batch_input[i] is the same memory location, every thread writes the same value. This is a benign data race.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the loop stride in Step 3 from blockDim.x (512) to blockDim.y (1). With blockDim.y=1, multiple threads redundantly write to the same output locations - thread 0 writes all 16384 elements, thread 1 writes elements 1-16383, etc. However, this is a benign race condition because every thread computes the identical output value for each element: they all read the same input value batch_input[i] and subtract the same log_sum_exp (which was correctly computed in Steps 1-2 and stored in shared memory). The race condition only affects performance (massive redundant work), not correctness. No input value pattern can make threads compute different values for the same output position.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation causes redundant writes of identical values. Since all threads compute batch_output[i] = batch_input[i] - log_sum_exp using the same batch_input[i] and the same log_sum_exp (from shared memory), the output is deterministically identical regardless of input values.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of CUDA kernels, include mutations that affect the values being computed (not just iteration patterns that cause benign races). Also consider testing with assertions or race detection tools to distinguish between equivalent-output races and true correctness bugs. The mutation testing framework could detect that blockDim.y=1 for 1D blocks and flag this as likely equivalent.
